label: abruptly narrowed
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's width decreasing suddenly, over a short distance, toward one end.
reason: The rule for 'narrowed' maps to PATO_0000417 tapered, but tapered is defined as narrowing gradually, so it does not fit an abrupt narrowing. This would sit beside tapered; FLOPO:0991169 clawed is a special case (narrowed into a stalk at the base).
This is the base of the part plus the quality flat (PATO_0000407), not a quality of its own. It fits the existing 'part of the bearer' slot.
'Huge leaves/fruit/root' means very large. This follows the rule enlarged → increased size, dropping the degree word.

A hyphenated compound means a value between its two words (playbook: 'X-Y' is between X and Y). One end is corymb-like (PATO_0002455). There is no term for 'paniculate', so that end has to be resolved first.

target: new: two values that both hold (compound, not continuum)
reason: Here the part is both wrinkled (PATO_0001810) and reticulate (FLOPO:0991100): wrinkles that form a network. That is not a value between two values, so the continuum reading would be wrong.

Placentas, sutures or fruit/seed apex 'intruded' means folded or projecting inward, which matches invaginated (an outer boundary folding in). The uses are mixed (placentas projecting into the cavity versus fruits indented), so confidence is low.
A degree adverb ('shortly aristate', 'shortly acute') that modifies another value. It is not a quality on its own.
Ascending is defined as directed gradually upward at an oblique angle, and 'arcuately' only describes the curve. The modifier is dropped, as in 'longitudinally fissured' → fissured.

'Commissural vittae' are on the commissure, the faces where the mericarps meet, so this is a position relative to another part. 'Commissural bundles' in leaf anatomy is a different sense, so this is uncertain.
A compound shape between elliptic (PATO_0000947) and rhomboid (PATO_0001938). It needs the continuum pattern, not a new term.
'Disk intrastaminal' means the disk sits inside the ring of stamens, a position relative to another part (the androecium). It is not a quality of the disk alone.
Caudate means having a tail or tail-like projection, and PATO lists 'tailed' as a related synonym. The length word ('long') is dropped or recorded as a degree.
Bearing a single head: a count of 1 capitulum inflorescence (PO_0030121) per stem or branch.
'Non glabres' negates glabrous. In the 'glabrous except for the rachis/lip' examples, the excepted part gets the negated value.
A compound shape between obovate (PATO_0001936) and rhomboid (PATO_0001938).

label: polygamo-monoecious
definition: A polygamous quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its bearing bisexual flowers together with both staminate and pistillate flowers on the same individual.
reason: A standard glossary term, more specific than polygamous (FLOPO:0991177) and in line with monoecious (FLOPO:0991071). A matching 'polygamo-dioecious' class is likely to be needed later.
Says that a region (alar cells, a phyllary zone) has a clear boundary with its neighbour. It needs the region and what it is set off from, and no existing term fits it safely.
A hyphenated compound between spreading (PATO_0104356) and erect (PATO_0000622), which is the continuum pattern of the playbook. The in-between angle is roughly ascending (PATO_0104355).

label: sweet
definition: A flavor quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a taste like that of sugar.
reason: PATO has flavor but no live taste values (its taste terms are obsolete), and fruit taste is a common flora character. 'Sweetish' itself is sweet plus the approximate-value pattern (docs/odp/01-approximate-value.md).
With three small lobes: a count of 3 lobes. It goes with the existing rule lobulate → lobed (PATO_0001979).

label: caducous
definition: A shedability quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's falling off early, soon after it is formed or has served its function.
reason: 'Caduceus' is a misspelling of caducous. PATO's deciduous terms describe a plant that sheds parts, not the part that falls, and FLOPO:0991181 marcescent is the matching class already under shedability.
Unthickened means not thickened. PATO_0000591 increased thickness has 'thickened' as a synonym.
Two values together: marked with fine lines (a pattern quality like FLOPO:0991206 streaked) and white (the colour of the lines, not of the part). It needs a pattern for the colour of a marking.
Columellate means having a columella. PO_0025230 covers fruit and moss-capsule columellae; the lichen apothecium examples are outside PO's scope.
A vague statement about how far a root or branch system spreads, or about the species' range. It is not a definite quality of the part.

label: pseudo-terminal
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's arising laterally, in the axil of the uppermost leaf or just below the apex, so that it appears terminal.
reason: A standard term for inflorescences: neither terminal (PATO_0002476) nor plainly axillary (FLOPO:0991000). It is consistent across four floras in two languages.
The part has markings, and the markings are purple. The colour belongs to the markings, not the whole part, so this uses the same new pattern as 'white-lineate'.
A compound shape between elliptic (PATO_0000947, which has 'ellipsoid' as a synonym) and cylindrical (PATO_0001873).
The examples say it directly: 'seeds without endosperm', 'sans endosperme'.

label: geophytic
definition: A herbaceous quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its surviving the unfavourable season as an underground storage organ, such as a bulb, corm, tuber or rhizome, that bears the renewal buds.
reason: A standard life-form term. It fits as a narrower case of herbaceous (parts above ground die back to the rootstock), although the 'geophytic shrublet' example stretches that parent.
